description:
A father refuses to speak a single word to his brilliant son for 15 years, not out of hatred, but as an act of love. That terrifying paradox sits at the heart of Chaim Potok's 1967 masterpiece, The Chosen.

In this analytical breakdown, we examine the clash between two fathers, two boys, and two worldviews in 1940s Brooklyn. From the explosive softball game that nearly blinds Reuven Malter to Danny Saunders's secret nights devouring Freud, we unpack why Reb Saunders weaponized absolute silence to carve a compassionate soul out of an arrogant, razor-sharp intellect.
